page: Microsoft Azure D8pls_v7 is an arm64-based virtual machine belonging to the Dplsv7 series, provisioned via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 8 dedicated virtual processor cores matched with 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server configuration does not include local disk storage and contains no discrete graphics processing units, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent disk requirements.

Hardware efficiency stems from its lean memory allocation and power-efficient ARM architecture. By reducing the memory footprint per core relative to standard 1:4 general-purpose profiles, the instance avoids resource overhead for workloads that do not require extensive in-memory indexing or large cache pools. Similarly, the absence of local ephemeral disks allows operators to provision only the external storage performance tiers necessary for their specific runtime environment.

The D8pls_v7 is designed for compute-bound tasks operating within modest memory envelopes. Typical workload deployments include continuous integration and deployment agents, microservices architectures, stateless application hosting, batch computing routines, and web servers that utilize remote block storage.
